title: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Gopinath Ravan Deshmukh on 15 March, 2016

United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Gopinath Ravan Deshmukh on 15 March, 2016

                                    1                   F.A..No.:812/2014




                                Date of filing :16.12.2014
                                Date of order :15.03.2016
MAHARASHTRA STATE CONSUMER DISPUTE REDRESSAL
COMMISSION,MUMBAI, CIRCUIT BENCH AT AURANGABAD.

FIRST APPEAL NO. :812 OF 2014
IN COMPLAINT CASE NO.: 270 OF 2011
DISTRICT CONSUMER FORUM : LATUR.

United India Insurance Co.Ltd.,
Tilak Nagar, Main Road, Latur,
Through its authorised signatory/
Divisional Manager,
Osmanpura, Aurangabad.                   ...APPELLANT


VERSUS

Gopinath S/o Ravan Deshmukh,
R/o Borgaon Kale,
Tq. & Dist.Latur.                        ...RESPONDENT.



           CORAM :      Mr.S.M.Shembole, Hon`ble Presiding Judicial
                        Member.

Smt.Uma S.Bora, Hon`ble Member.

Present : Adv.Mr.S.G.Chapalgaonkar for appellant, Adv.Mr.V.R.Jain for respondent.

O R A L JUDGMENT (Delivered on 15th March 2016) Per Mr.S.M.Shembole, Hon`ble Presiding Judicial Member.

1. This appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 16.9.2014 passed by Dist.Consumer Forum, Latur partly allowing complainant's claim in C.C.No.270/2011 directing appellant/original opponent insurance company to pay to the complainant amount of insurance Rs.4,12,500/- and further compensation Rs.5000/-

2 F.A..No.:812/2014

towards mental agony and Rs.2000/- more towards cost of the proceeding.

(For the sake of brevity appellant United India Insurance Co.Ltd. is herein after referred as the opponent insurance company and respondent Mr.Gopinath Deshmukh as the complainant)

2. Brief facts giving rise to this appeal are that:-

Complainant Gopinath was the owner of tanker bearing registration No.MH-24F-6959. It was insured with opponent insurance company for the period from 30.3.2010 to 29.3.2011. During the subsistence of the insurance policy, in the night on 23.6.2010 insured tanker stolen away by unknown person. On the same day information was given to the Police Station, Murud and on the basis of information F.I.R. was lodged against unknown person. Police made investigation but the vehicle is not found. Thereafter on 23.9.2010 complainant gave intimation to the opponent insurance company and submitted insurance claim. But opponent insurance company by its letter dated 7.6.2011 informed the complainant repudiating his claim on the ground that intimation was not given immediately after the incident of theft and therefore committed fundamental breach of terms and conditions of the policy. It was also informed that complainant has not taken due care of insured vehicle etc. Therefore alleging deficiency in service on the part of opponent insurance company, complainant has filed consumer complaint claiming amount of Rs.5,50,000/- with 12% interest, compensation Rs.20,000/- towards mental agony and Rs.5000/- more towards cost of the proceeding.

3. In response to the complaint notice, opponent insurance company appeared before the Forum and by its written version resisted the complaint contending inter alia that it has rightly repudiated the claim as the complainant has committed fundamental 3 F.A..No.:812/2014 breach of terms and conditions of the policy. It has denied all other adverse averments made by the complainant and submitted to dismiss the complaint.

4. On hearing both side and considering evidence on record District Consumer Forum held that opponent insurance company has committed deficiency in service by repudiating complainant's claim. In keeping with these findings Dist.Consumer Forum partly allowed the complainant's claim as noted above.

5. Feeling aggrieved by that judgment and order, opponent insurance company came to this Commission in appeal.

6. We heard counsel for both side and perused the written notes of argument submitted by them. We have also perused the copy of impugned judgment and order, copies of complaint, written version, repudiation letter, insurance policy and other documents.

7. Almost all the facts except the contention of opponent insurance company that complainant committed fundamental breach of terms and conditions of the policy by not giving intimation of theft of vehicle immediately and further not taking due care of the vehicle, are not disputed. Therefore the crux in this matter is as to whether complainant has committed fundamental breach of terms and conditions of the policy or not?

8. Mr.S.G.Chapalgaonkar learned counsel appearing for the opponent insurance company pointing out from the copy of insurance policy submitted that as per the terms and conditions of the policy it was obligatory on the part of complainant to give intimation about theft of vehicle immediately. But complainant gave intimation on 23.9.2010 i.e. after 3 months of the incident of theft. Further he has submitted that though as per survey report the insured vehicle is 4 F.A..No.:812/2014 stolen away by using original key, wrong information was given to the police to the effect that the vehicle was stolen away by using duplicate key. It is further submitted that complainant has not taken due care of the insured vehicle. According to him driver of the vehicle should not have kept the original key in the cabin. Thus according to Mr.Chapalgaonkar, complainant has committed fundamental breach of terms and conditions of the policy. Therefore opponent insurance company has rightly repudiated the claim. But District Consumer Forum without considering all these undisputed fact committed error in holding that opponent insurance company has committed deficiency in service by wrongly repudiating the claim. He has also supported his submission by relying on the following decisions of Hon'ble National Commission.

i) United India Insurance Co.Ltd. -Vs- Sachin Bhimrao Kamble dated 13.5.2015 in revision petition No.670/2015.
ii) Jaspal Kaur & Anr. -Vs- New India Assurance Company Ltd. dated 17.3.2015 in revision petition No.1670/2014.
iii) Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd. -Vs- K.K.Valsalan, 2014 STPL(CL) 2030 NC.

9. As against the submission of Mr.Chapalgaonkar learned counsel for the opponent insurance company , Mr.V.R.Jain learned counsel for the complainant submitted that though there was some delay in giving intimation to the opponent insurance company, it has given reasonable explanation. But opponent insurance company has not considered his explanation. According to him while given intimation dated 23.9.2010 complainant has mentioned that due to his disturbed mental condition there was delay. According to him claim cannot be repudiated on such ground of delay. He has also tried to support his contention by relying on the decision of Hon'ble National Commission in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd. -Vs- Kulwant Singh, 5 F.A..No.:812/2014 IV(2014) CPJ 62(NC). It is also submitted that there was no negligence on the part of complainant in taking due care of the insured vehicle. But relying on the survey report opponent insurance company has falsely contended that complainant was negligent in taking due care of the vehicle. According to him though the original key of the vehicle was kept in the vehicle's cabin, the cabin was locked. But key was obtained by thieves by breaking open cabin lock or by using duplicate key. It is submitted that opponent insurance company has not appointed any surveyor or investigator. But we find little force in the submission of Mr.Jain advocate appearing for the complainant. Because though original key of the vehicle was kept in the safe locked cabin, it was obligatory on the part of complainant to give intimation to the opponent insurance company about theft of insured vehicle. When the complainant could give information to the police immediately after the incident of theft, at the same time he could give intimation to the opponent insurance company. Therefore the contention of complainant that due to disturbed mental condition he could not give intimation, cannot be accepted.

10. In the case of Kulwant Singh (supra) in which counsel for the complainant relied on Hon'ble National Commission observed that no prejudice would have caused to the opponent insurance company due 4-5 days delay in receiving intimation of theft when plausible explanation was given by the complainant. But in the present case when undisputedly there was three months delay in giving intimation to the opponent insurance company it cannot be accepted no prejudice would have caused to the opponent insurance company. Therefore decision of Hon'ble National Commission in the case of Kulwantsingh cannot be applicable to the present case. On the contrary decisions of Hon'ble National Commission on which learned counsel for the opponent insurance company relied on are perfectly applicable to the present case. Because in the case of Sachin Bhimrao Kamble (Supra) though there was 5-6 days delay in giving intimation, 6 F.A..No.:812/2014 Hon'ble National Commission held that complainant committed breach of terms and conditions in not giving intimation of theft immediately. Likewise in the case of Jaspal Kaur(Supra) that there was delay of 11 days in giving intimation to opponent insurance company Hon'ble National Commission relying on decision dated 17.8.2010 of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. -Vs- Parvesh Chander Chadha held that "respondent/complainant was duty bound to inform the opponent insurance company about theft of vehicle immediately after incident on account of delay intimation, opponent insurance company deprived of his legitimate right to get an inquiry conducted into the alleged theft of the vehicle and make an endeavour to recover the same". Further in the case of K.K.Valsalan Hon'ble National Commission held that it was obligatory on the part of complainant to take due care of the vehicle keeping keys in the vehicle and leave the vehicle unattended amounts to deficiency in service.

11. Thus we have given our anxious thoughts to the argument advanced by counsel for both side and also facts of the case and we find that complainant committed breach of terms and conditions in not giving intimation of theft to the opponent insurance company immediately. Further complainant also acted negligent by leaving vehicle unattended keeping key in the cabin. But it appears from the copy of impugned judgment and order that District Consumer Forum without appreciating the evidence on record properly committed error in holding that opponent insurance company committed deficiency in service by repudiating the complainant's claim. Such findings of the District Consumer Forum are being erroneous cannot be sustained.

12. For the foregoing reasons appellant insurance company succeeds and appeal deserves to be allowed. Hence the following order.

7 F.A..No.:812/2014 
                                  O   R     D   E   R


   1. Appeal is allowed.

2. Consumer complaint No.270/2011 stands dismissed.

3. Having regard to the peculiar facts of the case we direct the parties to bear their own cost.

4. Copies of the judgment be supplied to both the parties.
